name: Familial Normophosphatemic Tumoral Calcinosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Familial Normophosphatemic Tumoral Calcinosis

criteria.description: Presence of periarticular calcified masses predominantly around large joints
Normal serum phosphate levels without evidence of hyperphosphatemia
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance
Exclusion of secondary causes of tumoral calcinosis such as chronic renal failure or metabolic disorders
Identification of mutations in genes associated with normophosphatemic tumoral calcinosis (e.g., SAMD9)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of periarticular calcified masses with normal serum phosphate levels and positive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of secondary causes of tumoral calcinosis and may be supported by genetic testing.

pathognomonic.notes: Firm, painless masses typically around hips, shoulders, and elbows

pathognomonic.symptomName: Normal serum phosphate levels despite calcinosis
searchTerms: normal phosphate blood levels despite calcium lumps
phosphate levels normal with calcium deposits

common.symptomName: Joint stiffness near affected calcified masses

searchTerms: small lumps under skin near joints

common.notes: Serum calcium remains within normal limits

occasional.symptomName: Limited joint mobility due to mass effect
searchTerms: limited joint motion due to masses

occasional.symptomName: Mild pain or discomfort at mass sites
Local skin ulceration over calcified masses
occasional.notes: Rarely occurs due to pressure necrosis
searchTerms: ulcers on skin above calcified areas

rare.symptomName: Joint deformities due to chronic calcinosis
searchTerms: joint deformities from long-term calcium buildup

rare.notes: Rarely, masses compress adjacent nerves causing neuropathy
searchTerms: nerve pain or weakness from compression
neurological symptoms due to mass effect

imaging: Radiographs showing periarticular lobulated calcified masses
CT or MRI demonstrating well-defined calcifications without bone involvement
other: Histopathology showing calcified amorphous deposits with fibrous capsule

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in GALNT3 or FGF23 genes
Associated with chronic renal failure or metabolic disorders
Abnormal serum phosphate or calcium levels

redFlags: Signs of secondary infection (redness, warmth, fever)
Neurological deficits suggestive of nerve compression
